newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Incitec mulls fertiliser plant expansion.
newsitem.headline: Incitec mulls fertiliser plant expansion.

text.p: Chemicals and fertiliser group Incitec Ltd said on Monday it was conducting feasability studies into a A$120 million upgrade of its urea plant at Gibson Island near the Queensland capital of Brisbane.

Incitec officials said a decision on whether to proceed would depend on a detailed assessment of future demand for nitrogen-based fertilisers and explosives as well as the availability of competitively-priced natural gas.

They confirmed a report in Business Queensland, a weekly newspaper, quoting managing director Jim Babon as saying the plant would require 30 percent more fuel over and above the quantity already contracted from Queensland producers.
Urea is used as a fertiliser, as animal food and the making of synthetic resins.
Incitec officials said the company produced about 220,000 tonnes of urea annually but also imported substantial quantities, depending on the season.
Incitec is a 72.7 percent subsidiary of ICI Australia Ltd which earlier announced growth plans for its Asian operations including paints and explosives.
